question: Which factor is most important to look at first when choosing an operating system for work?

options.A: The physical weight of the computer keyboard and mouse
options.B: The aesthetic color of the computer desktop background wallpaper
options.C: The specific software applications required to complete job tasks
options.D: The number of video games pre-installed on the hard drive

explanation: Software compatibility is critical because specialized tools must be able to run properly on the chosen operating system platform. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T1#BMP123_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does the fetus get enough magnesium if the mother's dietary intake is low?

options.A: The fetus absorbs magnesium through the mother's skin
options.B: The fetus makes its own magnesium inside the amniotic sac
options.C: The placenta actively transports available magnesium across to the fetus
options.D: The placenta blocks all magnesium to protect the mother

explanation: The placenta prioritizes getting minerals to the fetus even when maternal reserves are low. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T8#BMP118_U2_T8_h3)

question: What happens when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back for too long without a hip tilt?

options.A: Leg blood flow increases and causes cramps
options.B: The baby stops moving completely
options.C: The heavy uterus presses on major blood vessels and lowers blood pressure
options.D: Her breathing becomes very deep and easy

explanation: Pressure on the main blood vessels reduces blood return to the heart, making the mother dizzy and lowering blood flow to the baby. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is accurate documentation of a perineal repair important in clinical practice?

options.A: It replaces the need to check the woman's vital signs
options.B: It guides ongoing care and tracks the healing progress
options.C: It is required primarily for hospital financial audits
options.D: It prevents the mother from feeling any postpartum pain

explanation: Detailed notes inform other health workers about the extent of trauma and the type of repair, guiding future assessments. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T6#BMP212_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is a chest wound dressing taped on only three sides after an accidental chest tube removal?

options.A: It helps the skin heal faster without leaving a permanent scar
options.B: It makes it easier for the doctor to put a new tube in quickly
options.C: It stops blood from soaking through the outer layers of gauze
options.D: It allows trapped air to escape and prevents tension pneumothorax

explanation: A three-sided dressing acts like a valve, letting air out when the patient coughs or breathes out, but sealing shut when they breathe in. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T11#BMP125_U1_T11_h6)

question: What are the three classic signs of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Jaundice, ascites, and pruritus
options.B: Bradycardia, bradypnea, and hypotension
options.C: Amenorrhea, hirsutism, and obesity
options.D: Polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia

explanation: High blood sugar causes excessive urination, excessive thirst, and increased hunger, which are the classic signs of diabetes. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T1#BMP216_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is it important to mention an attached file inside the main text of your email?

options.A: To alert the recipient to look for the file even if they miss the icon
options.B: To make the email message pass through anti-virus software faster
options.C: To increase the download speed of the attached document
options.D: To legally force the recipient to print out the document

explanation: Mentioning the attachment in your writing ensures the reader knows a file is included even if the icon is small or hidden on their screen. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T3#BMP123_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following structures does not have its own surrounding membrane?

options.A: Golgi apparatus
options.B: Mitochondria
options.C: Endoplasmic reticulum
options.D: Ribosome

explanation: Ribosomes are simple structures made of RNA and protein that build proteins for the cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h2)

question: What compound does fluoride form when it joins with tooth enamel?

options.A: Potassium phosphate
options.B: Calcium carbonate
options.C: Fluorapatite
options.D: Sodium chloride

explanation: Fluoride binds with tooth minerals to create fluorapatite, which resists decay much better than regular tooth enamel. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the main function of tertiary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing highly specialized medical and surgical care
options.B: Providing temporary shelter for displaced community members
options.C: Handling routine immunizations and community health talks
options.D: Managing basic normal deliveries at the village level

explanation: Tertiary centers sit at the top of the referral chain to handle complex cases that lower levels cannot manage. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h1)

question: How does narrative analysis differ from thematic analysis?

options.A: Narrative analysis relies entirely on laboratory blood work and numerical statistics
options.B: Narrative analysis looks at complete individual life stories rather than breaking text into codes
options.C: Narrative analysis only uses closed-ended survey questions with fixed answers
options.D: Narrative analysis avoids recording interviews and relies on memory alone

explanation: Narrative analysis keeps a person's life story in chronological order rather than chopping the text up into separate codes. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T3#BMP225_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does giving the tetanus vaccine to a pregnant woman protect her newborn baby?

options.A: It permanently prevents the infant from ever cutting their skin later in life
options.B: It kills all bacteria living inside the delivery room environment instantly
options.C: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta to provide early protection after birth
options.D: The vaccine travels directly into the baby's bloodstream through amniotic fluid

explanation: Vaccinating the mother prompts her immune system to create protective antibodies which cross the placental barrier to shield the newborn. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to build lasting immunity against dangerous childhood diseases?

options.A: Administering recommended routine childhood vaccinations
options.B: Allowing the infant to consume nutrient-rich colostrum
options.C: Deliberately exposing a child to wild natural infections
options.D: Receiving protective antibodies via transplacental transfer

explanation: Intentionally exposing children to natural infections is unsafe because it risks severe complications and illness compared to standard immunizations. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T9#BMP111_U6_T9_h5)

question: Which gland releases oxytocin into the bloodstream when the cervix stretches during labor?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Posterior pituitary gland
options.C: Adrenal cortex gland
options.D: Anterior pituitary gland

explanation: Nerve impulses from the stretched cervix signal the brain, which causes the posterior pituitary gland to release stored oxytocin. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T3#BMP212_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main role of the pelvic ligaments during pregnancy and labor?

options.A: To produce the hormones that soften the cervix before delivery
options.B: To actively push the baby down through the birth canal during contractions
options.C: To limit excessive movement of the pelvic bones while allowing necessary stretch
options.D: To completely lock the joints so no movement can occur

explanation: Ligaments provide structural stability, preventing the pelvis from over-separating while still permitting slight give during birth. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T1#BMP210_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is Hepatitis E infection particularly dangerous when contracted by a pregnant woman through contaminated water?

options.A: It triggers sudden high blood pressure and maternal seizures
options.B: It prevents the placenta from producing progesterone entirely
options.C: It carries an exceptionally high mortality rate during pregnancy
options.D: It causes immediate and permanent blindness in the unborn fetus

explanation: Physiological changes during pregnancy make women uniquely vulnerable to severe liver failure from Hepatitis E. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h5)

question: How are major groups of fungi primarily distinguished from one another?

options.A: Their exact color when viewed without a microscope
options.B: The specific geographic region where they grow
options.C: The specific human organ they infect first
options.D: Their methods of sexual and asexual reproduction

explanation: Fungal groups are classified largely based on the specific structures they use to produce spores during reproduction. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T1#BMP116_U3_T1_h2)

question: Where should a mother who has just survived a severe PPH be transferred for close monitoring?

options.A: Intensive Care Unit or High Dependency Unit
options.B: General postnatal ward with routine care
options.C: Her private home with oral medications
options.D: Outpatient clinic for follow-up next week

explanation: Mothers recovering from major blood loss need close, continuous monitoring of their vital signs and fluid balance in a high-care unit. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h7)

question: A staff nurse working exclusively in the hospital operating theater would most likely join which specialty body?

options.A: Accident and Emergency Nurses Association of Nigeria
options.B: National Association of Paediatric Nurses of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses in Academia
options.D: Perioperative Nurses Association of Nigeria (PTONAN)

explanation: Perioperative nurses work in surgical suites and operating theaters, making PTONAN the appropriate specialty association for them. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT related to nerve physiology in obstetric care?

options.A: Using magnesium sulfate to calm central nervous system irritability in eclampsia
options.B: Calculating the exact daily caloric intake required for fetal bone growth
options.C: Applying local anesthetics for pain relief during perineal tear repair
options.D: Administering epidural anesthesia to block pain pathways during labor

explanation: Caloric intake and fetal bone development deal with nutrition and growth, not nerve signal transmission. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h7)

question: Why are barbiturates much more dangerous than modern sedatives during an overdose?

options.A: They permanently damage the heart muscle on contact
options.B: They cannot be reversed by any known medical antidote
options.C: They cause immediate kidney failure within minutes
options.D: They lack a ceiling effect for respiratory depression

explanation: Barbiturates continue to suppress breathing as the dose increases, which can easily lead to fatal respiratory arrest. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T3#BMP124_U3_T3_h3)

question: A ward manager notices high rates of incomplete partographs and holds a quick refresher session on proper plotting. Which management function does this represent?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Organizing
options.C: Staffing
options.D: Controlling

explanation: Reviewing documentation standards and correcting performance gaps through training is a classic example of controlling. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T5#BMP312_U1_T5_h6)

question: How do hospital managers use information gathered from maternity registers?

options.A: To advertise private maternity services online
options.B: To decide which staff members receive promotions
options.C: To track health trends and plan resource allocation
options.D: To determine personal grocery allowances for doctors

explanation: Summary data from registers provides essential statistics that help plan public health needs and distribute hospital supplies. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why are pregnant women more at risk for low blood oxygen levels when breathing becomes difficult?

options.A: The placenta absorbs all available oxygen before it reaches maternal lungs
options.B: They have increased oxygen demand combined with reduced functional residual capacity
options.C: Their red blood cells completely stop carrying oxygen during the third trimester
options.D: Their tidal volume drops to zero whenever they lie down flat

question: Why must the body keep dissolved mineral ions in the blood tightly regulated?

options.A: Electrolytes are required to make white blood cells daily
options.B: High ion levels will turn all plasma proteins solid
options.C: Even small imbalances can disrupt nerve conduction and heart rhythm
options.D: Mineral ions are the only substances that provide energy

explanation: Nerves and muscles depend on balanced electrolyte levels to function correctly. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T1#BMP111_U5_T1_h4)

question: How should non-reassuring fetal heart patterns be handled initially during an episode of maternal DKA?

options.A: Stop all maternal insulin infusions until the baby's heart rate normalizes
options.B: Focus primarily on aggressive maternal fluid resuscitation and metabolic stabilization
options.C: Administer high-dose oxytocin to speed up vaginal delivery
options.D: Perform immediate emergency Caesarean section regardless of maternal stability

explanation: Fetal distress in DKA is usually secondary to maternal acidosis and dehydration, so correcting the mother's metabolic state is the best way to rescue the fetus. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T3#BMP216_U2_T3_h7)

question: What physical sign is commonly seen on the lower back of a newborn with spina bifida occulta?

options.A: An exposed mass of nervous tissue
options.B: A tuft of hair or skin dimple
options.C: A large fluid-filled transparent sac
options.D: A complete absence of the skin

explanation: Spina bifida occulta is hidden beneath the skin, but small skin markers like a patch of hair, a birthmark, or a dimple often give a clue to its presence. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T3#BMP220_U2_T3_h2)

question: How can a midwife clinically distinguish a simple blocked duct from infectious mastitis?

options.A: Whether the mother is a primigravida or a multiparous woman
options.B: The location of the pain within the left versus right breast
options.C: The presence of systemic symptoms like fever and chills in mastitis
options.D: The total volume of milk produced during a single feeding session

explanation: While both conditions involve localized pain, systemic signs such as fever and body aches only appear when inflammation progresses to true mastitis. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is a common professional barrier faced when introducing midwife-led care models?

options.A: Universal agreement among doctors to handle all normal births
options.B: Interprofessional friction and misunderstanding of midwifery scope
options.C: Mandatory retirement age of twenty-five for all practicing midwives
options.D: Complete lack of pregnant women willing to use maternity services

explanation: Resistance from medical colleagues who misunderstand midwifery autonomy is a frequent hurdle when establishing these care models. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the minimum hourly urine output needed for a patient on magnesium sulfate?

options.A: 30 milliliters per hour
options.B: 250 milliliters per hour
options.C: 10 milliliters per hour
options.D: 100 milliliters per hour

explanation: Making at least 30 ml of urine per hour shows the kidneys are clearing the drug and preventing buildup. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h4)

question: A postpartum mother spends two hours every morning cleaning baby bottles over and over. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Report her immediately to social services for unsafe care
options.B: Validate her feelings gently and check for perinatal OCD
options.C: Tell her to stop cleaning because germs are harmless
options.D: Prescribe an antidepressant medication right away in the clinic

explanation: Gentle listening and validation build trust, helping the midwife assess compulsive behaviors without shaming the mother. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T7#BMP223_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which part of a joint capsule makes the lubricating synovial fluid?

options.A: Fibrous outer layer
options.B: Synovial membrane
options.C: Periosteum lining
options.D: Articular cartilage

question: What two values are needed to calculate the simple range of a dataset?

options.A: The highest value and the lowest value
options.B: The median value and the standard deviation
options.C: The arithmetic mean and the total sample size
options.D: The upper quartile and the lower quartile

explanation: The range is found simply by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T1#BMP225_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient asks how long sperm can survive and wait for ovulation in the female tract. What is the best response?

options.A: Up to five days
options.B: Exactly twenty-four hours
options.C: More than two weeks
options.D: Only a few minutes

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis compared to medical asepsis?

options.A: To make hospital linen smell fresh and clean
options.B: To reduce only the number of visible dirt particles
options.C: To eliminate all microorganisms completely from an area
options.D: To prevent airborne droplets from traveling across rooms

explanation: Surgical asepsis creates a sterile zone where no living germs are present. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why must midwives be cautious when relying solely on clinical physical exams for nutrition?

options.A: Pregnant women never display physical symptoms of poor nutrition
options.B: Physical examinations are illegal for midwives to perform in primary care clinics
options.C: Physical signs usually only show up when a nutrient deficiency is already quite advanced
options.D: Clinical signs are identical for every single vitamin deficiency known to science

question: What is the primary purpose of ward governance in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To assign daily kitchen and cleaning duties to junior staff
options.B: To strictly reduce the number of hours nurses spend on duty

explanation: Ward governance creates the structural framework needed to ensure high clinical standards and protect patients. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T4#BMP312_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which movement happens when the baby tucks its chin tightly against its chest?

options.A: Restitution
options.B: Flexion
options.C: Extension

question: What simple tool do midwives commonly use during community outreach to check for acute malnutrition in children?

options.C: Urine dipstick test strip
options.D: Standard blood pressure cuff

question: A midwife manager expects 20 percent more deliveries next year. What should she use to estimate future supply needs?

options.A: Past spending records combined with the expected patient volume increase

options.C: Only the funds left over in the current month's bank account

question: A pregnant woman is worried about taking her prescribed anti-anxiety pills. How should the midwife reply?

options.A: Dismiss her worries because doctors know best

question: Why must a patient finish all prescribed antibiotics even after their throat pain goes away?

options.A: Leftover tablets turn into dangerous toxins over time.
options.B: Incomplete courses cause penicillin allergies.
options.C: Stopping early can allow surviving bacteria to cause a relapse.
options.D: Unused pills will expire quickly in storage.

question: What is a key part of community reintegration programs for VVF survivors?

options.A: Full exemption from community leadership roles

question: Why is magnesium sulfate preferred over standard anticonvulsants for preeclampsia?

options.B: It completely eliminates the need to monitor blood pressure
options.C: It cures the underlying placental disease instantly

question: How do presumptive signs differ from probable signs?

options.A: Presumptive signs are subjective sensations reported by the woman
options.B: Presumptive signs are always confirmed using laboratory tests
options.C: Probable signs are felt exclusively by the pregnant woman
options.D: Probable signs only appear during the postpartum period

question: What is the main role of the sympathetic nervous system on the bladder while it is storing urine?

options.A: Sending pain signals directly to the cerebral cortex during filling

question: What ethical duty requires a midwife to keep a patient's personal health information private?

options.A: Altruism
options.B: Confidentiality
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Veracity

question: At what point does the supervision and monitoring phase of clinical delegation officially end?

options.A: Only when a patient makes a formal complaint
options.B: The exact moment you give the initial instruction
options.C: After the task is completed and feedback is provided
options.D: When the staff member goes home for the day

question: What does a severe degree of skull bone molding on the partograph mean?

options.C: Rapid dilation of the cervix without any obstruction
options.D: Normal descent of the fetus through a wide birth canal

question: What is the main action of a cardiotonic drug like digoxin on the heart?

question: Which joints should be included when immobilizing a fractured long bone?

options.C: Only the joint located directly below the fracture

question: What is the recommended action when a midwife notices a strange glitch in the maternity ward software?

options.A: Attempt to rewrite the programming code of the software application

question: Which type of calcium stays tightly regulated and normal in maternal blood during pregnancy?

question: Why is failing to document routine repositioning considered a serious professional issue?

question: Which abdominal muscle layer is the deepest and acts like a natural corset?

question: What is the main goal of antenatal education in Nigerian midwifery practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital delivery fees for families

options.C: To replace traditional birth attendants completely with private doctors

question: What is the primary purpose of hospital infection surveillance systems?

options.A: To collect and analyze data for detecting outbreaks
options.B: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.C: To calculate daily patient feeding budgets
options.D: To design new advertisements for the maternity wing

explanation: Surveillance is designed to track infection trends and spot unusual clusters of disease early so action can be taken. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h5)

question: A woman at 32 weeks comes in with sudden, painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Placenta praevia
options.B: Uterine rupture
options.C: Normal bloody show

question: A patient with narrowed heart arteries does heavy work on a hot afternoon and gets severe chest pain. What most likely caused this?

question: Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood directly into the systemic circulation?

options.A: Left atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Right atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

question: Which change happens to the sarcomere when a muscle contracts?

question: What is the very first priority for a nurse arriving at a poisoning scene?

options.A: Ensuring the safety of the environment
options.B: Writing down the exact time of exposure
options.C: Washing the patient's skin with soap

question: Why does pethidine act faster when given intravenously compared to intramuscularly?

question: A postpartum mother says she stopped her prescribed antibiotics after three days because her wound stopped hurting. What is your best response?

question: A non-pregnant woman has a calculated Body Mass Index of 28.5. How should a midwife classify this result?

question: What is the most important message to share with the family of a woman recovering from postpartum psychosis?

question: Which of these is a key feature of pure inquiry research?

question: What is the main role of a midwife when it comes to nutrition during antenatal care?

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical complication for a mother after long-term rupture of membranes?

question: Besides physical injuries, what other type of experience does childbirth trauma include?

question: A midwife wants to mobilize busy market women for a maternal health campaign. What is the most effective approach?

question: What does the presence of specific IgM antibodies in a pregnant woman's blood test usually indicate?

question: What is the main job of the kidneys in the body?

question: What is the specific pharmacological antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity?

question: Why is a urinary catheter inserted during the emergency care of a patient with a ruptured uterus?

question: What are the abnormal tissue tunnels called that can connect the bowel to the skin or other organs?

question: Why are nurses and midwives uniquely positioned to provide continuous health education?

question: Why must deworming programs always be paired with teaching about environmental sanitation?

question: What happens during a high or total spinal block complication?

question: What type of questions should make up the majority of an interview guide?

question: Which nutrient is especially important for providing building blocks for collagen during tissue repair?

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like at its peak fertility?

question: What is the simple definition of a wound?

question: Which common laboratory test checks urine or swab samples to detect chlamydia and gonorrhoea?

question: Why is the Billings method helpful for women with irregular menstrual cycles?

question: What is the main goal of providing antenatal care right inside community settings?

question: What triggers the mid-cycle LH surge through positive feedback?

options.B: Sustained high levels of estrogen from the mature follicle
options.C: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.D: High levels of progesterone secreted by immature follicles

explanation: Unlike the rest of the cycle where estrogen suppresses hormone release, peak estrogen levels paradoxically trigger a burst of GnRH and LH. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h6)

question: How many times a day should a breastfed baby aged 6 to 8 months usually get solid meals?

options.A: 6 to 8 times daily
options.B: 2 to 3 times daily
options.C: Only when crying
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Guidelines recommend offering solid foods 2 to 3 times a day alongside breast milk for infants aged 6 to 8 months. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does the acronym ISBAR stand for in clinical handovers?

options.A: Injury, Speed, Breathing, Ambulance, Report
options.B: Immediate Signs, Blood pressure, Action, Result
options.C: Investigation, Summary, Bed assignment, Review
options.D: Introduction, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: ISBAR is a widely accepted communication tool that ensures all critical patient facts are transmitted clearly without confusion. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T11#BMP110_U7_T11_h7)

question: Why does heavy scarring inside the liver cause serious health problems?

options.A: It blocks the normal flow of blood through the liver
options.B: It causes the gallbladder to burst open
options.C: It immediately stops all stomach acid production
options.D: It floods the lower limbs with extra bone marrow

explanation: Scar tissue creates a roadblock, making it hard for blood to flow through the liver properly. This builds up pressure in nearby blood vessels. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary tool a midwife uses to build trust and gather clinical information?

options.A: Advanced laboratory testing
options.B: Routine physical restraint
options.C: Strict hospital protocols
options.D: Effective communication

explanation: Communication is the core method midwives use to connect with patients, understand their needs, and collect vital health history. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T3#BMP110_U3_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant woman in her third trimester reports constant fatigue and poor weight gain despite eating her usual pre-pregnancy portions. What is the most likely physiological explanation?

options.A: Her increased BMR and fetal demands require more calories than her current intake.
options.B: Her digestive tract has slowed down to absorb less food.
options.C: Her thyroid gland has completely stopped producing hormones.
options.D: Her body has lowered its metabolic rate to store more fat.

explanation: Late pregnancy raises energy requirements significantly, so eating normal pre-pregnancy amounts will lead to a deficit, causing fatigue and poor weight gain. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason midwives use magnesium sulfate to prevent seizures in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Eclampsia
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the standard medicine used to prevent and manage seizures linked to eclampsia. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T7#BMP213_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the most common reason for bleeding and loss in early pregnancy?

options.A: Chromosomal abnormalities in the fetus
options.B: Heavy physical labor by the pregnant woman
options.C: Maternal consumption of spicy foods
options.D: Acute urinary tract infections

explanation: Most first-trimester pregnancy losses happen because of natural genetic mistakes during cell division, not because of anything the mother did. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is usually the earliest and most common sign that a person is developing COPD?

options.A: Severe sharp chest pain during resting hours
options.B: Progressive shortness of breath during physical activity
options.C: Uncontrollable sudden episodes of dry coughing
options.D: Sudden complete loss of voice and hoarseness

explanation: Feeling short of breath when walking or doing chores is typically the first noticeable symptom that prompts someone to visit a clinic. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T9#BMP125_U1_T9_h3)

question: How does the onset of HHS usually compare to diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)?

options.A: HHS develops much more slowly over weeks
options.B: HHS appears suddenly within a few minutes
options.C: DKA develops over several weeks instead
options.D: Both conditions always start simultaneously

explanation: While DKA can develop quickly within hours, HHS builds up slowly over days or weeks, causing severe fluid loss before it is noticed. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T4#BMP216_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is treating protozoal infections in pregnancy trickier than in non-pregnant patients?

options.A: Protozoa during pregnancy multiply much slower than in normal hosts
options.B: Parasites in pregnant women never develop drug resistance
options.C: Medications must be carefully evaluated for potential risks to the developing fetus
options.D: Standard adult dosages are completely ineffective in pregnant women

explanation: The safety of the unborn baby limits which drugs a midwife or doctor can give, balancing the mother's health with the baby's protection. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T11#BMP124_U4_T11_h1)

question: How should midwives balance institutional rules in a maternity ward?

options.A: Ignoring hospital protocols in favor of total patient freedom
options.B: Allowing patients to manage their own complex surgical procedures
options.C: Protecting the patient's dignity while maintaining clinical safety
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital rules without listening to complaints

explanation: Midwives must respect personal dignity and agency while following necessary safety guidelines. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h3)

question: Where does a drug administered by the oral route primarily enter and absorb from?

options.A: The muscular tissue
options.B: The gastrointestinal tract
options.C: The venous blood supply
options.D: The respiratory system

explanation: Oral medications travel through the mouth into the stomach and intestines where absorption into the bloodstream takes place. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T2#BMP120_U2_T2_h1)

question: How does communication usually flow during the main part of a traditional lecture?

options.A: Constant collaborative debate among all attending learners
options.B: Unidirectional flow from the lecturer to the students
options.C: Peer-to-peer teaching led exclusively by senior students
options.D: Strictly digital communication through mobile messaging apps

explanation: Traditional lecturing involves the instructor talking and the students listening, which is a one-way path of sharing information. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h2)

question: An antenatal ward is noisy with visitors talking loudly and metal carts squeaking. A midwife asks visitors to lower their voices and oils the cart wheels. Which Nightingale principle is she demonstrating?

options.A: Conducting a scientific study on hospital acoustics
options.B: Administering sedatives to calm restless patients
options.C: Managing noise and physical disturbances in the environment
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visitor bans during labor

explanation: Unnecessary noise causes real physiological stress to a recovering patient, making noise control a key part of environmental management. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T6#BMP110_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is a main benefit of delayed cord clamping for a healthy newborn?

options.A: Immediate closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.B: Faster clearance of lung fluid
options.C: Improved iron stores and higher blood volume
options.D: Prevention of all heart defects

explanation: Waiting to clamp the cord allows extra blood to flow from the placenta, giving the baby extra blood volume and vital iron reserves. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T5#BMP210_U5_T5_h4)

question: How can midwives help survivors who need legal protection?

options.A: By arresting the alleged perpetrator within the hospital premises
options.B: By issuing legally binding protection orders directly from the clinic
options.C: By connecting survivors to legal aid services and social support agencies
options.D: By serving as the official prosecuting attorneys in court trials

explanation: While midwives do not provide legal services themselves, they play a crucial bridging role by linking survivors to appropriate legal and social support networks. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h5)

question: What does a statistical power level of 80% mean for a study?

options.A: There is an 80% chance that the research funding will cover all costs.
options.B: Only 20% of the target population has the medical condition of interest.
options.C: There is an 80% chance of detecting a real clinical difference if it exists.
options.D: Eighty percent of the participants will complete the entire study protocol.

explanation: Statistical power is the probability that a study will successfully spot a genuine effect when one is actually present. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T7#BMP225_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of a physical hazard in a labor ward?

options.A: Emotional burnout from handling difficult relatives
options.B: Inhalation of strong chemical sterilizing agents
options.C: Accidental needlestick injuries from a syringe
options.D: Wet floors causing slips and falls

explanation: Slippery floors due to fluids or cleaning water represent environmental physical hazards that can cause direct physical injury. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T2#BMP126_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing an electrocardiogram, or ECG, during pregnancy?

options.A: To test the mother's blood sugar and iron levels
options.B: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid
options.C: To evaluate the electrical activity of the heart
options.D: To check if the baby has a congenital heart defect

explanation: An ECG records the electrical signals passing through the heart muscle to check its rhythm and overall function. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T1#BMP125_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why are pregnant women and neonates considered especially vulnerable to foodborne illnesses?

options.A: Their digestive tracts completely lack normal microflora
options.B: They consume a much larger volume of food than adults
options.C: They process harmful bacteria faster than the general population
options.D: Their immune systems struggle to cope with foodborne pathogens

explanation: Physiological changes during pregnancy and immature immune systems in newborns make it harder for their bodies to fight off infections. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T5#BMP117_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why must a midwife cut the suture thread close to the skin surface during removal?

options.A: To prevent pulling contaminated surface thread through the tissue track
options.B: To ensure the scissors remain sharp enough for the next procedure
options.C: To make sure the discarded thread stays long enough to reuse later
options.D: To prevent the patient from feeling any cold air on the wound

explanation: The exposed part of the thread collects bacteria from the air and skin surface; pulling that dirty section through the flesh can seed an infection. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which government agency coordinates the Expanded Programme on Immunization in Nigeria?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration
options.B: Federal Ministry of Education and Training
options.C: Nigerian Medical and Dental Council
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main government body tasked with organizing and managing primary healthcare services, including routine immunization across Nigeria. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T3#BMP117_U3_T3_h3)

question: What do we call glands that release their secretions directly into the bloodstream without using ducts?

options.A: Salivary glands
options.B: Ductless glands
options.C: Exocrine glands
options.D: Sweat glands

explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts to carry their secretions, releasing hormones straight into nearby blood vessels instead. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h1)

question: What primary physical process causes the postpartum uterus to shrink back to its normal size?

options.A: Complete shedding of the pelvic floor
options.B: Continuous myometrial contractions
options.C: Rapid increase in estrogen levels
options.D: Immediate closure of the cervix

explanation: Strong uterine muscle contractions actively reduce the size of the organ and seal off open blood vessels at the placental site during involution. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following temperature readings falls into the moderate hypothermia range?
explanation: Moderate hypothermia covers core body temperatures between 32.0°C and 35.9°C. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T3#BMP220_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which public health strategy is recognized as one of the most cost-effective ways to protect infants from deadly infections?

options.A: Mass surgical interventions
options.B: Routine immunization programs
options.C: Broad-spectrum antibiotic sales
options.D: Hospital-based quarantine

explanation: Vaccines prevent children from contracting severe and often fatal infectious diseases before they are exposed. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T2#BMP117_U1_T2_h4)

question: What happens to the mother's response to insulin in late pregnancy?

options.A: Insulin sensitivity decreases to keep more sugar for the baby
options.B: Insulin sensitivity increases to clear blood sugar rapidly
options.C: All blood sugar is turned into muscle protein
options.D: The pancreas stops making insulin completely

explanation: Late pregnancy insulin resistance leaves more glucose available in the maternal blood for placental transfer. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why is it important to write down exact error codes when a computer crashes?

options.A: They point directly to the specific cause or failing component
options.B: They serve as a password backup
options.C: They speed up internet connection rates
options.D: They automatically repair damaged files

explanation: Error codes provide precise technical clues that help technicians identify whether the issue is hardware or software related. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T4#BMP123_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary laboratory method used to confirm an intestinal tapeworm infection?

options.A: Urinalysis using chemical reagent strips
options.B: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels
options.C: Chest X-ray imaging of the lung fields
options.D: Stool microscopy for eggs or proglottids

explanation: Stool microscopy allows laboratory technicians to spot characteristic tapeworm eggs or passed segments. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which situation is a clear example of using telemedicine?

options.A: Distributing printed health pamphlets during a community immunization drive
options.B: Performing a routine surgical procedure inside a sterile operating theater
options.C: Providing healthcare services when distance separates the provider and client
options.D: Conducting an in-person physical pelvic examination at a local clinic

explanation: Telemedicine specifically bridges geographical distance by using electronic communication tools for care delivery. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why should a pregnant woman be tilted slightly to her side during a physical examination?

options.A: To prevent the heavy uterus from compressing major blood vessels
options.B: To make it easier to measure her height and weight accurately
options.C: To stop her from falling asleep on the examination couch
options.D: To encourage the baby to move into a breech presentation

explanation: Lying flat on the back allows the heavy uterus to press on the main blood vessels, which can lower blood pressure and cause dizziness. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T1#BMP125_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do social stressors like a lack of family support impact a pregnant woman's mental health?

options.A: They reduce the physical discomfort of morning sickness
options.B: They automatically normalize her blood pressure levels
options.C: They increase her vulnerability to chronic stress and anxiety
options.D: They prevent any form of postpartum hormonal shifts

explanation: A strong support system cushions against stress, whereas isolation and hardship amplify feelings of fear and overwhelm. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T4#BMP223_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical use of cholinergic drugs like bethanechol in postpartum care?

options.A: Treating urinary retention
options.B: Speeding up cervical dilation
options.C: Stopping severe postpartum bleeding
options.D: Lowering high blood pressure

explanation: Bethanechol helps stimulate the detrusor muscle of the bladder, making it useful when a mother cannot pass urine after giving birth. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T4#BMP124_U2_T4_h5)

question: Where is the perineal body anatomically located in the female pelvis?

options.A: Above the pubic symphysis
options.B: Behind the rectum against the sacrum
options.C: Between the vagina and the anus
options.D: Within the broad ligament of the uterus

explanation: The perineal body sits right in the middle between the lower vagina and the anal canal, acting as a meeting point for pelvic floor muscles. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T7#BMP210_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a proactive risk management activity on a labor ward?

options.A: Calculating the total monthly expenditure on delivery kits
options.B: Interviewing a patient who experienced a surgical site infection
options.C: Writing a detailed report after a postpartum hemorrhage emergency has concluded
options.D: Checking that emergency drugs are unexpired and oxygen tubing is intact at shift change

explanation: Inspecting equipment and supplies before they are urgently needed prevents emergencies from turning disastrous. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T4#BMP312_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of the spinal cord in connection with the brain?

options.A: Filtering waste products from nerve tissue
options.B: Making pregnancy hormones
options.C: Controlling the heartbeat rhythm
options.D: Acting as a signal highway between the body and the brain

explanation: The spinal cord carries messages from the body up to the brain, and sends movement commands back down from the brain to the body. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T2#BMP121_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which condition commonly causes "punched-out" lytic lesions in the flat bones of the skull?

options.A: Rickets
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Multiple myeloma
options.D: Osteomalacia

explanation: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells that frequently forms destructive, punched-out lesions in bones containing active red marrow like the skull. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T5#BMP111_U2_T5_h5)

question: What happens to the vaginal pH when the number of protective Lactobacilli drops a lot?

options.A: It remains perfectly stable because the cervix regulates the pH
options.B: It shifts entirely to a neutral balance that supports normal tissue repair
options.C: It becomes extremely acidic, killing off all bacteria completely
options.D: It becomes less acidic, which encourages harmful microbes to grow

explanation: When lactic acid goes down, the vaginal pH rises above 4.5. This creates an easy environment for bad microbes to multiply. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of a comprehensive PMTCT strategy?

options.A: Primary prevention of HIV infection in young women
options.B: Mandatory surgical sterilization for all infected women
options.C: Prevention of unintended pregnancies among positive women
options.D: Provision of antiretroviral prophylaxis to exposed infants

explanation: PMTCT respects reproductive rights and focuses on safe pregnancy planning. Forcing sterilization violates human rights. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T6#BMP221_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of natural active immunity?

options.A: Receiving a tetanus toxoid injection at the clinic
options.B: Getting a transfusion of maternal antibodies via breast milk
options.C: Recovering from a wild measles infection
options.D: Taking an intravenous course of broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Natural active immunity develops when your body mounts its own defense after contracting an illness naturally in the environment. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T7#BMP111_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is the medical term for the natural loss of muscle mass that happens as people get older?

options.A: Atherosclerosis
options.B: Osteomalacia
options.C: Sarcopenia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Sarcopenia describes the shrinking of muscle bulk and strength associated with aging, which lowers the body's overall energy needs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T7#BMP118_U3_T7_h1)

question: A patient is given a strong cholinergic medication. Which finding is most likely to be observed during assessment?

options.A: Inability to urinate due to bladder relaxation
options.B: A very fast resting heart rate and high fever
options.C: Dry mouth, constipation, and dilated pupils
options.D: Increased watery saliva and abdominal cramping

explanation: Cholinergic drugs stimulate secretions and smooth muscle activity, leading to lots of saliva and active bowel movements or cramps. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T4#BMP124_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main clue when a colonoscopy reveals 'skip lesions'?

options.A: It indicates that the disease is completely cured
options.B: It strongly points toward a diagnosis of Crohn's disease
options.C: It shows that only the rectal mucosa is involved
options.D: It proves the infection is caused by a specific parasite

explanation: Skip lesions mean healthy tissue sits right next to inflamed tissue, which is a classic sign that helps separate Crohn's disease from continuous conditions like ulcerative colitis. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which way does oxygen move during internal respiration at the tissue level?

options.A: From the skin surface out into the air
options.B: From tissue cells into the lung alveoli
options.C: From venous blood into arterial circulation
options.D: From tiny blood vessels into surrounding tissue cells

explanation: Internal respiration means oxygen is being delivered from the capillaries into the working cells of the body. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to check a pregnant woman's packed cell volume (PCV) at booking and around 32 weeks?

options.A: To measure the exact weight gain of the developing fetus
options.B: To detect and treat worsening anemia due to increased plasma volume expansion
options.C: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: To confirm the precise gestational age of the pregnancy

explanation: Blood volume increases greatly in pregnancy, often diluting red blood cells and leading to anemia that requires monitoring and treatment. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why should pregnant women be advised not to stop their asthma medications out of fear for the baby?

options.A: Asthma medications have zero side effects on human tissue
options.B: The placenta stores asthma drugs and feeds them directly to the baby
options.C: Uncontrolled asthma attacks cause dangerous oxygen deprivation for the fetus
options.D: Stopping medication causes permanent lung collapse in the mother

explanation: The danger of low oxygen from an untreated asthma attack is much higher than the small risks associated with standard, approved asthma medications. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T8#BMP125_U1_T8_h4)

question: What name is given to the slightly acidic film found on the surface of healthy skin?

options.A: Mucous layer
options.B: Acid mantle
options.C: Lipid plaque
options.D: Sebaceous crust

explanation: The acid mantle is the protective acidic coating on the skin that helps stop harmful germs from multiplying. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T4#BMP111_U4_T4_h3)

question: Where do thermal receptors in the body send their primary temperature signals?

options.A: Straight to the peripheral blood vessels
options.B: To the skeletal muscles for shivering
options.C: Directly to the sweat glands in the skin
options.D: To the hypothalamus in the brain

explanation: Temperature sensors all over the body send data back to the hypothalamus so it can take action to keep the body comfortable. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T5#BMP111_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why does giving an infant regular solid foods lower the birth control effectiveness of breastfeeding?

options.A: It directly stimulates the mother's ovaries to release an egg
options.B: It decreases the frequency and intensity of suckling at the breast
options.C: It neutralizes the hormonal feedback loop in the infant's digestive tract
options.D: It permanently stops the production of breastmilk within forty-eight hours

explanation: When a baby fills up on other foods, they breastfeed less often, which changes the mother's hormone levels and can bring back ovulation. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an objective test item?

options.A: Short paragraph explaining eclampsia
options.B: Long essay on postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Multiple-choice question
options.D: Clinical case study discussion

explanation: Multiple-choice questions have fixed, predetermined correct answers, making them strictly objective. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why might a surgeon remove a stitch or two from an infected surgical cut?

options.A: To test if the skin has finished healing completely
options.B: To make room for a new adhesive plaster dressing
options.C: To reduce the patient's overall body temperature
options.D: To allow trapped pus and fluid to drain out freely

explanation: Loosening a small part of the wound relieves pressure and lets infected fluid escape, helping the patient recover faster. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why do opportunistic fungal infections rarely cause severe disease in healthy people?

options.A: Normal bacterial flora actively kills all fungal spores
options.B: An intact immune system successfully controls the organism
options.C: Body temperature is too high for opportunistic fungi to survive
options.D: Healthy skin tissues produce natural antifungal oils

explanation: Opportunistic fungi are weak pathogens that require a compromised immune system or disrupted body defenses to establish deep or widespread infection. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T2#BMP116_U3_T2_h3)

question: When should you do the full physical check on a newborn?

options.A: Prior to the cutting of the umbilical cord
options.B: Within the first twenty-four hours of life
options.C: Only when the mother is discharged home
options.D: Exactly at one hour after delivery

explanation: Doing a thorough check within the first day helps catch any hidden health concerns early. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T2#BMP214_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is the accumulation of subcutaneous fat late in pregnancy important for a newborn baby?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for breast milk in the first week
options.B: It prevents the baby from breathing too quickly outside the womb
options.C: It allows the baby to float more easily inside the amniotic fluid
options.D: It provides insulation and helps regulate body temperature after birth

explanation: Subcutaneous adipose tissue acts as insulation against the cooler external environment and provides an immediate energy source for the newborn. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h4)

question: What are the four main parts of the upper limb?

options.A: Chest, back, thigh, and foot
options.B: Neck, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis
options.C: Shoulder, arm, forearm, and hand
options.D: Clavicle, scapula, humerus, and digits

explanation: These four distinct zones contain the muscle groups responsible for moving the upper extremity. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T10#BMP111_U3_T10_h1)

question: How do midwives and doctors diagnose unexplained antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: By confirming that the bleeding originates directly from fetal circulation vessels
options.B: When the patient refuses to undergo any routine physical examination during labour
options.C: When the bleeding stops completely without any medical or nursing intervention
options.D: After ruling out placenta praevia, abruption, and local tract lesions through examination and scan

explanation: Unexplained APH is a diagnosis made only after other known causes of bleeding have been checked and ruled out. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which pregnancy hormone relaxes smooth muscles and slows down bowel movements?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes the smooth muscles of the digestive tract, slowing down peristalsis and causing food and waste to move more slowly. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is surfactant production around the 24th week of pregnancy so important for a premature baby?

options.A: It lubricates the umbilical cord to prevent dangerous twists and knots
options.B: It helps red blood cells carry extra oxygen through the fetal blood vessels
options.C: It fights off bacterial infections inside the immature respiratory tract
options.D: It prevents the tiny air sacs in the lungs from collapsing during exhalation

explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension in the tiny lung air sacs, keeping them open so the newborn can breathe without struggling. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T5#BMP210_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why can synovial joints move much more than other joint types?

options.A: They possess a fluid-filled cavity separating the bone ends
options.B: They lack any form of structural stabilization or tissue support
options.C: They are completely fused together by solid bone tissue
options.D: They are anchored tightly by thick sheets of dense cartilage

explanation: A fluid-filled cavity separates the bones so they do not rub directly against each other during movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is the main job of a short-acting inhaler like salbutamol during an asthma flare-up?

options.A: To permanently destroy excess mucus-producing glands
options.B: To lower the pregnant woman's systemic blood pressure
options.C: To cure the underlying bacterial lung infection
options.D: To quickly relax constricted bronchial smooth muscles

explanation: Reliever inhalers work fast to open up tightened airways, making it much easier for the patient to breathe during a sudden attack. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T8#BMP125_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is a good example of objective clinical documentation?

options.A: Nothing unusual found anywhere on the body today
options.B: Skin pink, chest clear to auscultation bilaterally, patient alert
options.C: Normal checkup done without any problems at all
options.D: Patient looks completely okay and happy this morning

explanation: Objective documentation uses specific, measurable findings rather than vague personal opinions like 'okay' or 'fine'. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T1#BMP110_U6_T1_h8)
